title: fix: tighten community model monitoring
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Raises short-term and seven-day reliability floors to 75%, with fallback rescues still counted as successes.
- Adds repeated provider-failure hiding and sustained recovery checks; separates caller-wallet errors from provider-account outages.
- Checks audio/video/embedding health from real traffic; starts cycles 30 minutes after completion without changing image cadence or Discord cooldowns.
- Preserves safe text-error details and accepts case-only probe-marker changes. All 15 focused monitor tests pass; seven-day report dry-run against live data succeeded.
- Rollout: merge to main, then update the EC2 runtime and systemd unit from merged main.

gist.headline: The garden gets stricter
gist.blurb: The community-model watchtower now expects a sturdier bloom: 75% short-term and seven-day reliability, with successful fallback rescues counted fairly. It also knows the difference between a visitor’s wallet issue and a provider having a rough day.
gist.summary: Community model monitoring now enforces 75% short-term and seven-day reliability floors, hides repeatedly failing providers, verifies sustained recoveries, and measures audio, video, and embedding health from real traffic.
gist.impact: Users get a more dependable community model garden as unreliable providers are surfaced less often, healthy recoveries are confirmed over time, and fallback successes continue to count as successful requests.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden watchtower represents the stricter community-model monitor: Polli tends several code-plants labeled text, audio, video, and embeddings while a friendly CRT robot checks a 75% health gauge. Healthy plants glow and receive water from a fallback pipe, while repeatedly wilted provider plants are gently tucked behind a hedge until they recover; this conveys reliable routing without making failure the focus.
